title: WhatsApp MCP bridge -- T1005 unauthenticated media_path traversal file read
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-46555 (GHSA-7jj9-4qqq-4xc4,
CVSS 7.7 HIGH), a self-reported advisory for `whatsapp-mcp` -- a Model
Context Protocol server that lets Claude read/send WhatsApp messages.

Prior to 0.2.1, the `whatsapp-bridge` HTTP API listened on
`127.0.0.1:8080` with no authentication and no Host-header validation,
and its `/api/send` endpoint accepted an absolute `media_path` parameter
without confining it to a safe directory. The advisory names the
disclosed impact directly: an unauthenticated local caller (which, per
the advisory, "extends beyond processes the user explicitly launched" to
sibling MCP servers, IDE extensions, and tool-triggered flows sharing the
session) could read arbitrary files the user account can access -- SSH
private keys, browser session data, source code, dotfiles -- and
exfiltrate them as WhatsApp document attachments to the paired account.
The missing Host-header check additionally lets a remote attacker trigger
the same request via DNS rebinding from a webpage the victim visits.

Detection logic flags a request to `/api/send` whose `media_path` field
is an absolute path (or contains a `..` traversal segment) rather than a
filename confined to the bridge's own media directory -- the fix
specifically introduces path confinement, so a request the fixed version
would reject is the discriminator.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (verygoodplugins,
via GHSA and NVD), fixed in v0.2.1.
